mcqs.q: Can a device ever be 100 percent efficient?
options: A well-designed device can be 100 percent efficient by eliminating all friction.
Efficiency above 100 percent is possible if the device extracts ambient energy.
In practice, no — some energy is always transferred to less useful stores (e.g. heat to surroundings).
Power is the energy used over the lifetime of a device.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between energy and power?
options: Power is the energy used over the lifetime of a device.
Energy and power are the same — both describe how much fuel something uses.
Energy is measured in joules; power is the rate of energy transfer, measured in watts (joules per second).
Low-frequency light doesn't have enough mass to push electrons out of the metal.

mcqs.q: Why does increasing the intensity of light below the threshold frequency not eject electrons?
options: Each photon's energy is below the work function; many low-energy photons can't combine to eject an electron.
Low-frequency light doesn't have enough mass to push electrons out of the metal.
Enough low-frequency photons should eventually eject an electron if you wait long enough.
Efficiency above 100 percent is possible if the device extracts ambient energy.
